rounds.text: The most critical flaw in Trans India House Impex Ltd is the alarming collapse in cash generation, evidenced by an operating cash flow of Rs -51.05 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -51.08 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32], resulting in a dismal cash conversion ratio of -33.59x against reported profit [E30]. This severe disconnect is compounded by dangerously bloated working capital requirements, specifically highlighted by excessively high debtors stretching to 744 days [E61]. Furthermore, insiders are rapidly abandoning the equity, with promoter holdings plummeting by 31.50 percentage points down to just 27.68% [E37]. Market sentiment matches this internal retreat, as the stock languishes at a relative-strength rating of 0, trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a 12-month return of -68.8% [E45, E46, E47]. Profitability remains weak and substandard, evidenced by a low 3-year median return on equity of 6% [E24] and explicit warnings that the company may be capitalizing interest costs [E60]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing sales and profit growth, trades at a low price-to-book ratio of 0.36x, and has successfully reduced its borrowings down to Rs 17.22 Cr [E2, E15, E19, E35, E54].
